- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 10–15% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days); adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for final 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth; use 3–5 day moving average of true values to anchor forecast mid-range.
